Reference Architecture

          
The 6 Pillars Glossary

        

        

          

        

      

      

        
All (6)

        
The Engine

        
The Wires

        
The Brain

        
The Society

        
The Armor

        
The Output

      

      

        

        

          

            
The Wires

            
#01

          

          
Model Context Protocol (MCP)

          

            

What:
 An open standard to connect AI models to external tools and internal databases.

            

Analogy:
 The universal USB-C port for artificial intelligence.

            

Why it matters:
 Connect your tools once and use them with any modern AI agent.

            
Takeaway: Standard protocols beat vendor lock-in every time.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Engine

            
#02

          

          
Tokens

          

            

What:
 The atomic pieces of words that language models read and write.

            

Analogy:
 Lego bricks or syllables of machine language.

            

Why it matters:
 Token count directly dictates your cloud bills and model speed.

            
Takeaway: Tokens are compute currency. Keep context trimmed.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Engine

            
#03

          

          
Context Window

          

            

What:
 The maximum number of tokens an AI can process at one time.

            

Analogy:
 The physical surface area of the desk where the AI works.

            

Why it matters:
 When overloaded, earlier instructions drop off or degrade in precision.

            
Takeaway: A bigger desk helps, but a clean desk prevents hallucinations.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Brain

            
#04

          

          
Skills & Rules Hierarchy

          

            

What:
 Modular instruction folders loaded only when specifically invoked.

            

Analogy:
 Standard Operating Procedure binders kept neatly on a shelf.

            

Why it matters:
 Keeps the base prompt concise while unlocking deep specialized knowledge on demand.

            
Takeaway: Load knowledge surgically, never all at once.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Society

            
#05

          

          
Orchestrator-Worker Loops

          

            

What:
 Dividing a multi-step job between specialized sub-agents with bounded scope.

            

Analogy:
 A general contractor supervising a certified electrician and a plumber.

            

Why it matters:
 Eliminates single-thread context bloat and prevents hallucination spirals.

            
Takeaway: Specialized small agents beat monolithic mega-prompts.

          

        

        

        

          

            
The Armor

            
#06

          

          
Falsifiable Verifiers

          

            

What:
 Independent deterministic checks that must be able to fail and catch errors.

            

Analogy:
 A smoke detector that you regularly trigger with test smoke.

            

Why it matters:
 A verification step that cannot fail is merely decorative theater.

            
Takeaway: The verifier must never be the producer.
